title: fix(service-storage, plugin-security): every member can attach files to the records they edit — storage contributes its own attachment set to the member baseline
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu25rjuLxNgaKr1YUx8UMXzr)_

Fixes #32754

## 维护者速读

- 问题：成员能编辑自己的记录，却不能往上面挂附件（403）：没有任何权限集给附件对象授权，附件的行级守门根本轮不到判。
- 改法（按裁定 B）：存储服务自带一个只有「读 + 新建」附件的权限集，经 `everyone` 发给每个登录成员；`member_default` 一字未改（ADR-0090 D9）。安全插件新增一个只在启动期开放的贡献接口来收这个集。
- 条件 ①：四道门（写规则、读可见性、下载的父记录检查、每对象的附件开关）全部在位才贡献；缺任何一道就不发，并在启动日志里点名缺哪道（第四道是契约复审第 1 轮补上的）。条件 ②：接口只收贡献者自己登记的对象、只收读和新建，拒通配、其它权限位、行策略、别的包的对象和启动后的调用，每次收下或拒收都记日志，每种拒收各有一条 pin。ADR-0090 那句不在本 PR（另走 Tier H）。
- 条件 ③ 写进 changeset：升级后，已有附件对能读父记录的成员重新可见；成员可以给自己能编辑的记录挂附件；能读不能编辑的成员现在拿到 `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS`（仍是 403）；编辑、删除附件仍要显式授权。外部用户、agent 自身、`fallbackPermissionSet: null` 的部署、不带存储服务或缺门的宿主都不变；代成员操作的 agent 受成员和自身 scope 双重约束，成员能挂它才能挂。
- 契约：`ISecurityService` 加一个可选成员 `contributePlatformBaselineSet`（Clause-② widening），不加元数据键，不碰 `docs/adr/`。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## What changes

**The grant.** `@objectstack/service-storage` now contributes its own permission set, `storage_attachment_member`: read and create on `sys_attachment`, nothing else. Every signed-in member holds it through the `everyone` anchor, beside `member_default`, as an additive baseline (ADR-0090 D5). `member_default` is unchanged (ADR-0090 D9).

The contribution happens in the storage plugin's `kernel:ready` handler, right after it installs the attachment row gates, and only when all four attachment gates are present: the write rule, the read-visibility gate, the download door's parent-record check and the per-object opt-in gate (`enable.files`). A kernel without one of them contributes nothing and says at warn level which gate is missing, so the object stays refused instead of ungated.

An agent principal gains nothing in its own right. An agent acting for a member is bounded by that member and by its own scope (ADR-0090 D10), so it can attach where the member can, within that scope.

**The seam.** `ISecurityService` gains an optional member, `contributePlatformBaselineSet(contributor, set)`. `SecurityPlugin` implements it with `PlatformBaselineSets`. Its rules:

- It is open only during boot. The window closes at `kernel:bootstrapped`.
- Each contributor gives one set, and the set carries only the closed keys.
- The set names only objects that the engine registry holds under the contributor's package.
- Each object entry carries only `allowRead` and `allowCreate`.

An admitted set is registered in the catalog under the contributor's package. When the deployment declares a member baseline, the set's name joins the one composed baseline array that every baseline reader shares: the data plane, explain, effective access, the describe fallback and the `everyone` definition. A set that joins after the `kernel:ready` derivation has begun causes one re-derivation of the anchor at `kernel:bootstrapped`. Every admission and every refusal is logged.

**Docs.**

- `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx` gains a "Who holds the object grant" section. Its callout and its enforcement summary now say that the baseline grants read and create, and that edit and delete need an explicit grant.
- The stale header of `attachment-access-hooks.ts` is fixed.

## Tests

| Ruling item | Pin |
|---|---|
| The grant lands only with all four gates present; no middleware means no grant | `storage-service-plugin.test.ts` (no middleware seam, no auth service, no hook seam, no per-object opt-in gate: each contributes nothing and the warning names the gate); `attachment-member-grant.test.ts` (each missing gate, no security service, no seam, a refusing seam, no baseline) |
| Each seam refusal | `platform-baseline-sets.test.ts`: unnamed contributor, closed window, row policy, every non-closed key, a second set, another contributor's name or a shipped name, no registry, no object, `'*'`, another package's object, an unregistered object, every bit other than read and create (even when `false`), non-boolean values, an entry that grants nothing, a malformed set, the registry refusing |
| Seam on a real kernel | `platform-baseline-sets.integration.test.ts`: a member reads and creates, and cannot edit or delete; explain names the set as an additive baseline; the `everyone` definition names it even though it landed after the derivation; the catalog holds it under the service's package; an external user gets nothing; an agent principal's own leg gets nothing; another package's object is refused on the real registry; the window is closed after bootstrap; `fallbackPermissionSet: null` admits the set and hands it to no one |
| Every contribution logged | same file: the admission line (set, contributor, grants, joined), the refusal line at warn (contributor, reason), and the no-baseline admission line |
| Upload-complete `attachTo` and the MCP `create_upload_link` door; an agent acting for the member on an OAuth token (admitted where the member and the token's scope both allow, refused where either does not); `ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS` on a readable-but-not-editable record; unreadable records' attachments stay invisible (list, total, by id); another user's attachment on a readable record is visible; `FILES_DISABLED`; explain names the storage set; a host without the storage service, and a host lacking one of the attachment gates, still answer 403 with no storage set | `member-attachment-baseline.dogfood.test.ts` (new, real stack) |
| Contract | `security-service.test.ts` (the member is optional, and its type carries only read and create); `registered-security-service-members.pin.test.ts` |

Two existing expectations move with the change:

- `print-service-archive`: an auditor who can read but not edit the invoice is now refused by the attach rule (`ATTACHMENT_PARENT_ACCESS`) instead of by the missing object grant. It is still a 403, and still raised before any mint or render.
- `catalog-reference-report` now sees two `kernel:bootstrapped` handlers, and the report is still the last.

## Verification

At head `e8eb97dc` (contract review round 1 addressed; `main` not merged again, merge-base `5fb79bc0`):

- Unit suites: `@objectstack/service-storage` (full: 79 files, 1486 passed); `@objectstack/plugin-security` (full at the round-1 head: 266 files, 6573 passed; the four suites this round touches, 72 passed); `@objectstack/spec` (`security-service.test.ts`, 30 passed). Package typechecks for plugin-security (including its test project), service-storage and dogfood. ESLint on the changed files is clean.
- Dogfood (real stack): the new suite (10 tests) plus the suites that touch attachments, explain or the `everyone` anchor, 53 files green (one skips for a missing enterprise package, as on `main`).
- Ablations. Each one reverts one guard, turns its pin red, and is then restored, with the blob equal to `HEAD` and a clean tree:
  - the read-visibility condition, the download-check condition and the opt-in gate condition (storage plugin pins);
  - the gates check (grant pins);
  - the owner check, the bit allowlist, the wildcard and row-policy refusals, and the window close (seam pins);
  - the seam's admission log line and its refusal log line (log pins);
  - the `kernel:bootstrapped` re-derivation (the `everyone`-definition pin);
  - the null-baseline join (its pins);
  - on the built artifact (service-storage `dist` rebuilt, with the marker proved present, then proved absent after the restore): with the grant disabled, 8 of the dogfood suite's 10 tests go red and both hosts without the grant stay green as controls; with the opt-in gate condition forced true, the host lacking that gate goes red.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` is current (`api-surface`, `export-origins` regenerated). `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` gives 128 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED.
